assessment.claims_audit: Retrospective executable counterexamples corroborate unchanged frozen source criteria; they are not added native grading cases or model inputs.
assessment.wide_test_failures: The captured model runs retain their three/eight wider-suite failures. A separate canonical-reference full-suite diagnostic has the same eight failing test IDs (466 pass, ten skip); native six-case grades remain separate and unchanged.
assessment.instruction_compliance_notes: Whitespace word counts show review overlength for Codegraph (656) and CodeNib (623). The frozen source rubric has no numeric word-count grading rule; retain these deviations without inventing a new post-hoc acceptance criterion. Minor line-number drift and broad safe-finalization wording remain interpretation limits, not a new grading protocol.
decision: No demonstrated whole-task advantage: CodeNib is slower than native/Codegraph, has more normalized usage and lower source acceptance.
CodeNib and Serena receive no voluntary MCP/CLI use; a raw time difference between native-fallback workflows is not backend efficacy.
All four patches make the same one-line production fix and pass all six hidden native cases, without erasing explanation errors or broader-suite failures.
The on-demand path avoids unused provider/graph preparation here; requested-body delivery is proven only by operator controls, not called by these model tasks.
Preserve both earlier cohorts and this complete development round. Do not repeat exposed tasks to seek a positive score.
Next engineering gate: establish useful voluntary use on a source-linked cross-file task and test concrete task-fit/tool-entry hypotheses before independent confirmation.
Two independent confirmation sets, representative update coverage and five-user consent/reuse remain open; enrollment 0/5 and no outreach.
